items.stem: Why is exact string match a poor metric for an open-ended question-answering assistant?

options.text: Many different wordings can be equally correct, so exact match penalises valid answers
options.rationale: Correct: open-ended outputs have many valid forms that exact match misses.

options.text: Exact match is too slow to compute at scale
options.rationale: It is cheap to compute; the problem is validity, not speed.
It is a simple string comparison needing no GPU.

options.text: Exact match only works for images
options.rationale: It applies to text; the issue is its strictness for open text.

items.explanation: Correct: open-ended outputs have many valid forms that exact match misses.

items.stem: Which TWO are sound practices when using an LLM as an automated judge? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Give the judge a clear rubric and reference answer where possible
options.rationale: Correct: an explicit rubric improves consistency and reduces drift.

options.text: Validate the judge against a sample of human-labelled cases
options.rationale: Correct: calibrating against human labels checks the judge's reliability.

options.text: Assume the judge is unbiased and never audit it
options.rationale: LLM judges have known biases and must be audited.

options.text: Let the judge grade its own model's outputs with no oversight
options.rationale: Self-grading without oversight risks inflated, unreliable scores.

items.explanation: Correct: an explicit rubric improves consistency and reduces drift.

items.stem: A model scores well offline but users report worse answers after a prompt change. What practice would have caught this before release?

options.text: A regression test comparing outputs on a fixed evaluation set across versions
options.rationale: Correct: regression testing flags quality drops before shipping.
Temperature changes randomness, not evaluation coverage.
Removing tests hides regressions rather than catching them.

options.text: Only testing on the easiest cases
options.rationale: Easy-only testing hides exactly these regressions.

items.explanation: Correct: regression testing flags quality drops before shipping.
